projects.name: KLA Fantasy
projects.desc: Development of the Kings League Americas Fantasy platform, with the goal of modernizing the gaming experience and building end-user loyalty.

sections.label: Overview
sections.title: All about KLA Fantasy
sections.body: A modern fantasy platform for the Kings League Americas: users build their ideal teams with player cards, compete every day and win tickets they can exchange for prizes like signed jerseys, exclusive experiences, trips and official merchandise, all inside an intuitive, dynamic platform designed so everyone has a chance to win.

sections.title: Challenge / Problem statement
sections.intro: Kings League Americas needed a fantasy experience that would raise fan engagement and build end-user loyalty throughout the season.
approach: Full integration with league data and live standings.

items.heading: Impact
items.body: Higher fan engagement and retention across the whole season.

sections.title: Conclusion
sections.body: We delivered a gaming experience that brought the league to life and connected fans with the brand.

projects.name: Hosting Wells
projects.desc: Redesign of the Hosting Wells elevator company website to modernize it and improve the user experience.

sections.label: Overview
sections.title: All about Hosting Wells
sections.body: Hosting Wells is a company specialized in the installation of elevators with German technology. We custom-built their official website: a modern, professional and responsive platform that clearly communicates their competitive advantages, services, guarantees and experience in the sector.

sections.title: Challenge / Problem statement
sections.intro: Hosting Wells needed a web presence that matched the quality of their engineering: their advantages, guarantees and track record weren't coming through online.
problems: The previous presence didn't reflect the company's quality and experience
Services and guarantees weren't clearly communicated
The site wasn't responsive or easy to update
approach: A modern, professional and fully responsive platform
Clear structure for services, guarantees and industry experience
A focus on efficiency, quality and specialized attention

items.heading: Positioning
items.body: The new site presents Hosting Wells as a specialized, reliable partner: German technology, clear guarantees and specialized attention front and center.

sections.title: Conclusion
sections.body: A clean, professional website that finally communicates Hosting Wells' competitive advantages. A second, more ambitious redesign (v2) is already in development.

projects.name: Copa Record
projects.desc: Design of the official mascot for the Copa Record México for commercial use and scalability in sports projects.

sections.label: Overview
sections.title: All about Copa Record
sections.body: Copa Record is a nationwide soccer tournament by Record Mexico that promotes the sport and crowns the best team in the country. We designed its official mascot, created to represent the energy, passion and competitive spirit of the event, connecting with players and fans alike.

sections.title: Challenge / Problem statement
sections.intro: Record needed an identity piece that could connect with players and fans nationwide, work across commercial materials and scale to future sports projects.
approach: A mascot that embodies the energy, passion and competitive spirit of the tournament
Versatile design ready for commercial use and scalable across sports projects
An interactive map prototype to plan courts, advertising and key areas of the event

items.heading: Impact
items.body: The mascot became the face of the tournament across its materials, and the interactive map prototype, presented to Club Deportivo Pachuca, helped plan courts, estimate advertising and propose ideas for key areas like the food court.

sections.title: Conclusion
sections.body: A mascot ready for commercial use and scalable to more sports projects, plus an interactive map that made integral event planning easier.

projects.name: Mundo Premier
projects.desc: An interactive experience for Aeromexico Rewards (formerly Club Premier) members, built with Santander's Toma Todo program to reward loyalty.

sections.label: Overview
sections.title: All about Mundo Premier
sections.body: We developed two dynamics for Aeromexico Rewards (formerly Club Premier) members, focused on building loyalty and letting them redeem points for prizes such as all-expense-paid trips. Mundo Premier was carried out in collaboration with Santander as part of the Toma Todo program.

sections.title: Challenge / Problem statement
sections.intro: Club Premier was looking for a strategic and reliable provider capable of developing interactive experiences for its advertising campaigns within a short development timeline and without any production errors, as any errors could lead to legal issues given the nature of the campaigns.
problems: Compliance with legal regulations governing games and sweepstakes for auditing purposes
approach: From day one, we offered a comprehensive solution in which the development timeline was tailored to the client's desired launch schedule. In this case, a two-month timeline for public launch, with zero margin for error during the launch.

Through constant communication with the client throughout the development process, extensive testing in a staging environment, and stress testing to handle high traffic volumes, we successfully achieved our goal.

items.heading: Development
items.body: Development of the final, tested version over a two-month period

items.heading: Over 60,000 users
items.body: An experience enjoyed by more than 60,000 users (Club Premier members, now Aeromexico Rewards)

items.heading: No errors
items.body: There were no production errors that could have affected the user's score. This was very important, as there were big prizes up for grabs, such as trips and SUVs.

items.heading: Successful report
items.body: Weekly reports were submitted to verify the authenticity of each user's games, including a review of high scores in relation to game duration and the number of games redeemed.

sections.title: Conclussion
sections.body: An experience that turned loyalty points into an opportunity to win big prizes, thereby further strengthening member loyalty

projects.name: Jokeland
projects.desc: A mobile game that expands the Pepito cartoon universe, letting players discover the characters' stories through interactive play.

sections.label: Overview
sections.title: All about Jokeland
sections.body: Jokeland is a mobile game created to connect with new audiences and expand the Pepito cartoon universe. Users learn the story of the characters in an interactive way, and the game works as a direct sequel to the animated series developed for social media.

sections.title: Challenge / Problem statement
sections.intro: The Pepito brand wanted to reach new audiences and extend its cartoon universe beyond the animated series on social media.
problems: The audience was limited to followers of the social media series
Fans had no way to go deeper into the characters' stories
approach: A mobile game that works as a direct sequel to the animated series
Interactive storytelling so players learn each character's story
Casual mechanics designed for broad audiences

items.heading: Engagement
items.body: Players discover the characters' stories through play, identify with them and keep the universe alive between episodes of the series.

sections.title: Conclusion
sections.body: Jokeland extended the Pepito universe into an interactive format and connected the brand with new audiences as a direct sequel to the animated series.

projects.name: Club Pepito
projects.desc: An online mini-game fair that positioned the Pepito brand with new audiences: play, earn tickets and redeem branded rewards.

sections.label: Overview
sections.title: All about Club Pepito
sections.body: Club Pepito was an interactive project designed to position the Pepito brand among new audiences through an online mini-game fair. Users earned tickets by playing and could redeem them for physical branded products and other rewards.

sections.title: Challenge / Problem statement
sections.intro: Pepito needed to position the brand with new audiences and turn passive exposure into active engagement.
problems: Traditional advertising wasn't generating engagement with new audiences
The brand needed a reason for users to come back
approach: An online mini-game fair (Corre Pepito, Aguas con la Lava and more)
A ticket system: play, earn tickets, redeem them for physical branded products
A trailer and social media push to drive traffic to the fair

items.heading: Loyalty loop
items.body: Play, earn tickets, redeem rewards: the fair turned brand exposure into a repeatable loop that kept users coming back.

sections.title: Conclusion
sections.body: Club Pepito turned brand positioning into play: users engaged with the mini-games and redeemed tickets for physical branded rewards, driving repeat visits.

items.q: What kinds of projects do you take on?
items.a: Anything that ends in working software. Web platforms, mobile apps, internal tools, integrations, e-commerce, and the occasional game or brand activation. If it can be built, it is in scope.

No. We scope every project around the problem in front of us, which is why two clients in the same industry rarely end up with the same system.

items.q: How small or large a project do you take?
items.a: From a one-month build to a platform we have run for years. We scale the team to the project rather than the other way round, so a small job does not get a small team's leftovers.
Often. We are the development team a lot of agencies need without hiring one, either behind the scenes or in front of the client.
One short call about what you need to happen. We come back with scope, timeline and cost, and once you agree we start building.

intro.heading: Who we are

JeeTP Studios builds custom software. Web platforms, mobile apps, internal tools, integrations, and the interactive work some clients need on top. We are developers, designers and strategists acting as the technical team for companies that do not have one, or that need a bigger one for a while.
There are no account layers between you and the people writing the code. Cost stays down, timelines stay honest, and we can size a team to a single project instead of a retainer.

overview.heading: What we have built

Loyalty platforms, sports products, elevator company websites, internal dashboards, commercial activations. Different industries, same job: work out what the business actually needs and build that.
Every project starts with one conversation about the problem. From there we set scope, timeline and cost, and then we build it.

Software should fit the business, not the other way round. Most of the bad systems we get called in to replace were built to a template someone had lying around.
